key_insight: Which larval trait matters most for settlement depends on the local flow regime: swimming speed dominates in fast flow, while body shape dominates in recirculating flow between ridges.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a physical basis for predicting and potentially designing flow-dependent recruitment in complex benthic habitats, with implications for coastal ecosystem management and habitat engineering.
method: Varied larval swimming speed and shape from circular to elongated
evidence_signal: Settlement success varied by up to an order of magnitude across trait combinations, showing strong flow-mediated sensitivity to larval properties.
watch_item: Results come from controlled simulations, so real-world performance may differ in natural environments with unmodeled turbulence, behavior, and biological variability.
paper_title: Flow regime determines whether larval settlement hydrodynamics are governed by swimming speed or shape
